text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Asia-Pacific leaders set action plan in motion by beginning to tear down trade and investment barriers in the region in five weeks.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong calls for thorough review of Singapore's economic competitiveness for next five to ten years.
- Singapore government will spend Singapore $50 million to help poor families enrol their children in the Before and After School Care programme.
- Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp plans to develop its fourth industrial park in Surabaya for Singapore $285 million and to be completed in year 2002.
- Interior designer Nobel Design Holdings shares debut at 62 percent above offer price of $0.33.
- Hong Leong Group teams up with the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation to acquire 80 percent stake in Hong Kong's JW Marriott Hotel for Hong Kong $2.2 billion.
- Stocks in Kuala Lumpur, Hong Kong and Singapore rise on strong instutitional buying.
- New York Stock Exchange identifies 20 to 25 Singapore companies as potential candidates for listing on Wall Street.
- Marco Polo Developments reports 62.2 percent rise in group net profit to Singapore $4.98 million for first half ending September 30.
- Creative Technology stands to gain from weakening yen.
- Shares of Sembawang Corp close unchanged at Singapore $7.75 amid sharply higher turnover of Jurong Shipyard Ltd.
